description: PostToolUse nudge table for the claude-tools nudge hook. Each entry attaches a convention reminder next to the tool result at the moment the convention becomes relevant, instead of relying on the model to recall the right one of ~40 skill descriptions.

nudges.message: You are editing a test file. claude-tools:testing-conventions applies: integration over unit for routes and repos, real infrastructure over mocks, no logger stubs, only external services stubbed. A test that cannot fail is worse than no test.

You added a log call. claude-tools:log-standards applies: log major process boundaries and failures, not trivial successes or hot loops. Message must be a static lowercase identifier — no interpolation, no raw error objects. Put every dynamic value in structured metadata, not the message string.

nudges.$comment: Anchored to a shell command boundary, with ^\s* so an indented command still matches. The `unless` flags are anchored too: bare '--amend' matched `git commit -m "fix --amend handling"` and suppressed the nudge.
nudges.message: Commit made. The git-per-task rule requires reaching the remote immediately — run `git pull --rebase` then `git push` now. No batching: each commit reaches origin so feedback stays continuous.

nudges.$comment: filePathPatterns restricts this to source files. Without it a markdown '# Heading' matched the '#' comment pattern, so editing CHANGELOG.md told the model it had added a code comment.
nudges.message: You added a code comment. The code-comments rule defaults to zero comments in every language — make the code self-explanatory instead. Keep it only if it carries a non-obvious workaround and why, a subtle invariant a reader would break, or a business rule / ticket link the code cannot express. Otherwise a rename or small refactor should remove the need for it.
